newsitem.title: USA: Trans-World fights Russia aluminium charges.
newsitem.headline: Trans-World fights Russia aluminium charges.

text.p: Trans-World Group plans to meet U.S. State Department officials on Monday in a bid to clear its name of persistent allegations linked to its activities in the Russian aluminium industry, lawyers for the company said.
Tyrone Fahner of Mayer, Brown & Platt said Trans-World will present a dossier to State Department officials that rejects three allegations made against the company.
The company will also raise concerns over a recent statement about the Russian aluminium industry made by the country's Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov in the Duma (parliament) earlier this month.
Fahner said Trans-World has already been cleared by the FBI and told it is not the target of any probe, thus paving the way for a meeting with the State Department.
Trans-World, whose management is based in London, also met last week a senior British Foreign Office official dealing with the Commonwealth of Independent States to discuss the same issues.
"The next step will be a meeting with Michael Heseltine (Deputy Prime Minister) and Ian Lang of the DTI (Department of Trade and Industry," said Eric Bettelheim, also of Mayer, Brown & Platt.
Trans-World says it is the biggest foreign investor in Russia outside the oil and gas industry, and employs 130,000 Russians, generating a big chunk of the company's $6 billion annual turnover.

Trans-World Group executive chairman David Reuben, flanked by lawyers and senior group executives briefed the press on Wednesday evening about the company's campaign to clear its name and stop what is saw as a potential threat to Trans-World's minority stake in two of Russia's aluminium smelters, Bratsk and Sayansk.
In his February 21 speech, Kulikov said Russia's aluminium industry should be protected from Western firms by tightening federal controls over tolling deals.
Russia should also consider slapping duties on imports of raw materials, Kulikov said.
Trans-World is a leading importer of alumina into Russia to be tolled smelted into aluminium metal for re-export.
The spat helped propel aluminium to a 14-month high on the London Metal Exchange on Tuesday due to concerns over supplies from Russia, the world's second biggest aluminium producer.
Lawyers for Trans-World said the company was seeking support from the U.S. and U.K. governments "so that Western businesses can continue to do business with us".

Bettelheim said Trans-World is rejecting three long-standing allegations -- that it defrauded the Russian Central Bank, that the deaths of three bankers were linked to the company's effort to wrestle back a 29 percent stake in the Krasnoyarsk smelter, and that it was supporting the Russian politician, Oleg Soskovets, who is seen as close to would-be president, Alexander Lebed.
Trans-World has also asked Kulikov, Anatoly Chubais, a leading Russian politician, and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin for talks regarding Kulikov's speech and the allegations.
